chapterNote: A national lament with no confession in it — the hardest kind. It opens with the catechism: our fathers told us what You did, how You drove out the nations with Your own hand and planted them, not by their sword but by Your right hand and the light of Your face, because You delighted in them. This generation has learned the lesson: I do not trust in my bow; in God we boast all day long. Then the hinge — yet You have cast us off. You do not go out with our armies; You sell Your people for nothing; You make us a byword and a head-shake among the nations. And the scandal: all this has come upon us, yet we have not forgotten You or been false to Your covenant — if we had, would God not search it out? For Your sake we are killed all day long, reckoned as sheep for slaughter. Paul quotes that line in Romans 8, between 'who shall separate us' and 'more than conquerors,' and that is where the church reads the answer this psalm never receives. Inside the psalm there is only the boldest prayer in the Psalter — wake up, why do You sleep, O Lord? — and the last word, which is the only ground left: ransom us for the sake of Your covenant love.

1.text: For the choir director. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil. O God, we have heard with our own ears; our fathers have recounted to us the work You worked in their days, in the days of old:
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] for the sons [ben] of Korah, Maschil [maskil]. We have heard [shama] with our ears [ozen], O God [Elohim], our fathers [ab] have told [saphar — recounted] us, what work [poal] You did [paal] in their days [yom], in the times [yom] of old [qedem].
1.notes: Elohim be-oznenu shamanu abotenu sipperu-lanu (H430, H241, H8085, H1, H5608): God, with our ears we have heard — our fathers RECOUNTED to us — the Deuteronomy 6:20-24 catechism, a father telling the exodus at the table; poal paalta bi-yemehem bi-yme qedem (H6467, H6466, H3117, H6924): the work You worked in their days, in the days of old. A maskil (H4905), a teaching psalm: the lesson begins with the old stories and then asks why they have stopped.

2.text: You, with Your own hand, drove out the nations and planted our fathers; You broke the peoples and sent them away.
2.amp: How You did drive out [yarash — dispossess] the heathen [goy — nations] with Your hand [yad], and planted [nata] them; how You did afflict [raa — break] the people [leom — peoples], and cast them out [shalach — sent away].
2.notes: attah yadekha goyim horashta va-tittaem (H3027, H1471, H3423, H5193): You — Your hand — dispossessed the nations and PLANTED them, our fathers — the planting of Exodus 15:17, which Psalm 80:8 turns into a vine; tara leummim va-teshallechem (H7489, H3816, H7971): You broke peoples and sent them off. The conquest told with God as the only subject: no Joshua is named.

3.text: For it was not by their sword that they took the land, and their own arm did not save them, but Your right hand and Your arm and the light of Your face — because You delighted in them.
3.amp: For they got not the land [eretz] in possession [yarash] by their own sword [cherev], neither did their own arm [zeroa] save [yasha] them: but Your right hand [yamin], and Your arm [zeroa], and the light [or] of Your countenance [panim — face], because You had a favour [ratsah — delighted] unto them.
3.notes: ki lo be-charbam yareshu arets u-zeroam lo-hoshiah lamo (H2719, H3423, H776, H2220, H3467): not by their sword did they possess the land, and their arm did not save them. Joshua 24:12 says the same: 'not with thy sword, nor with thy bow'; ki-yeminekha u-zeroakha ve-or panekha (H3225, H2220, H216, H6440): but Your right hand, Your arm, the light of Your face — ki retsitam (H7521): because You DELIGHTED in them. Grace as the cause of the conquest: Deuteronomy 7:7-8 in a hymn.

4.text: You Yourself are my King, O God; command the victories of Jacob!
4.amp: You are my King [melek], O God [Elohim]: command [tsavah] deliverances [yeshuah — salvations, victories] for Jacob [Yaaqob].
4.notes: attah-hu malki Elohim (H4428, H430): You, You are my King, O God — the singular 'my' in a national psalm: the king, or each singer, claiming the covenant personally; tsavveh yeshuot Yaaqob (H6680, H3444, H3290): COMMAND the salvations of Jacob — yeshuot, plural, victories on order. From memory (vv. 1-3) to petition in one line; the King who did it then is asked to issue the order again.

5.text: Through You we push our adversaries down; through Your name we trample those who rise against us.
5.amp: Through You will we push down our enemies [tsar — adversaries]: through Your name [shem] will we tread them under [bus — trample] that rise up [qum] against us.
5.notes: bekha tsarenu nenaggeach (H6862): through You we GORE our adversaries — the ox-verb of Deuteronomy 33:17, Joseph's horns; be-shimkha nabus qamenu (H8034, H947, H6965): in Your name we trample those who rise against us. The confidence is entirely borrowed: 'through You', 'in Your name'.

6.text: For I do not trust in my bow, and my sword does not save me.
6.amp: For I will not trust [batach] in my bow, neither shall my sword [cherev] save [yasha] me.
6.notes: ki lo be-qashti ebtach ve-charbi lo toshieni (H982, H2719, H3467): not in my bow do I trust, and my sword does not save me — verse 3's creed said in the first person by the current generation: they have learned the lesson the fathers taught. Which is what makes verse 9 so hard.

7.text: No — You have saved us from our adversaries, and You have put those who hate us to shame.
7.amp: But You have saved [yasha] us from our enemies [tsar — adversaries], and have put them to shame [bosh] that hated [sane] us.
7.notes: ki hoshatanu mi-tsarenu (H3467, H6862): for You have SAVED us from our adversaries — u-mesanenu hebishota (H8130, H954): and You have shamed our haters. Past victories credited to God alone, the way the fathers taught (v. 1); the psalm has been faithful to its catechism.

8.text: In God we have boasted all day long, and we will thank Your name forever. Selah.
8.amp: In God [Elohim] we boast [halal] all the day [yom] long, and praise [yadah — thank] Your name [shem] for ever [olam]. Selah [Selah].
8.notes: b-Elohim hillalnu khol-ha-yom (H430, H1984, H3117): in God we have BOASTED all the day — halal, the allowed boast of Psalm 34:2 and Jeremiah 9:24; ve-shimkha le-olam nodeh (H8034, H5769, H3034): and Your name forever we will thank. Selah — the last pause before the psalm turns over.

9.text: Yet You have cast us off and disgraced us, and You do not go out with our armies.
9.amp: But [aph — yet] You have cast off [zanach — rejected], and put us to shame [kalam — humiliated]; and go not forth [yatsa] with our armies [tsaba].
9.notes: aph-zanachta va-takhlimenu (H637, H2186, H3637): YET — You have cast off and humiliated us; ve-lo-tetse be-tsibotenu (H3318, H6635): and You do not go out with our armies — the ark that went before Israel (Numbers 10:35) now stays home. The hinge of the psalm: everything the fathers said God did, He has stopped doing, and the people cannot find the reason.

10.text: You make us turn back from the adversary, and those who hate us plunder at will.
10.amp: You make us to turn [shub] back [achor] from the enemy [tsar — adversary]: and they which hate [sane] us spoil for themselves.
10.notes: teshibenu achor minni-tsar (H7725, H268, H6862): You TURN us back from the adversary — the retreat is God's doing, as the advance was (v. 2); u-mesanenu shasu lamo (H8130): and our haters plunder 'for themselves' — the spoils Israel once took (Joshua 8:27) now taken from her.

11.text: You hand us over like sheep to be eaten, and You have scattered us among the nations.
11.amp: You have given [natan] us like sheep [tson] appointed for meat ['as sheep of meat', tson, the KJV margin]; and have scattered [zarah — winnowed] us among the heathen [goy — nations].
11.notes: tittenenu ke-tson maakhal (H5414, H6629): You give us 'like sheep of food', the margin's literal — mutton, not a flock; u-ba-goyim zeritanu (H1471, H2219): and among the nations You have WINNOWED us — zarah, the threshing-floor verb, chaff thrown to the wind (cf. Leviticus 26:33). Verse 22 will pick the sheep image up, and Paul will pick it up from there.

12.text: You sell Your people for nothing, and You made no profit on their price.
12.amp: You sell [makar] Your people [am] for nought ['without riches', hon, the KJV margin], and do not increase [rabah] Your wealth by their price [mechir].
12.notes: timkor-ammekha be-lo-hon (H4376, H5971, H1952): You SELL Your people 'without wealth', the margin's literal — for nothing — ve-lo-ribbita bi-mechirehem (H7235, H4242): and did not raise Your price on them: a fire-sale, no bidders. Isaiah 52:3 answers it: 'ye have sold yourselves for nought; and ye shall be redeemed without money.'

13.text: You make us a reproach to our neighbors, a mockery and a joke to those around us.
13.amp: You make [sum] us a reproach [cherpah] to our neighbours, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us.
13.notes: tesimenu cherpah li-shekhenenu (H7760, H2781): You SET us as a reproach to our neighbors — laag va-qeles li-sebibotenu: a mockery and a derision to those around us. Psalm 79:4 and 80:6 use the same three words for the same humiliation; the neighbors are Edom, Moab, Ammon, the cousins who enjoy it most (cf. Obadiah 12).

14.text: You make us a byword among the nations, a head-shake among the peoples.
14.amp: You make [sum] us a byword [mashal — proverb] among the heathen [goy — nations], a shaking of the head [rosh] among the people [leom — peoples].
14.notes: tesimenu mashal ba-goyim (H7760, H4912, H1471): You make us a mashal among the nations — a proverb, a cautionary tale, Deuteronomy 28:37's curse landing; menod-rosh ba-leummim (H7218, H3816): a head-shake among the peoples — the gesture of Psalm 22:7 at the cross.

15.text: All day long my disgrace is in front of me, and the shame of my face has covered me,
15.amp: My confusion [kelimmah — disgrace] is continually [yom — all the day] before me, and the shame [bosheth] of my face [panim] has covered [kasah] me,
15.notes: kol-ha-yom kelimmati negdi (H3117, H3639): all the day my humiliation is in front of me — u-boshet panai kissatni (H1322, H6440, H3680): and the shame of my face has COVERED me — boshet, the word the prophets swap in for Baal (Ish-bosheth): shame as a garment. The singular 'my' again: the nation's disgrace worn by one face.

16.text: because of the voice of the one who taunts and reviles, because of the enemy and the avenger.
16.amp: For the voice [qol] of him that reproaches [charaph — taunts] and blasphemes; by reason [panim] of the enemy [oyeb] and avenger [naqam].
16.notes: mi-qol mecharef u-megaddef (H6963, H2778): from the voice of the taunter and the reviler — mi-pene oyeb u-mitnaqqem (H6440, H341, H5358): from the face of the enemy and the avenger — the pair of Psalm 8:2, where God's strength out of babes' mouths silences them. Here no one is silencing them.

17.text: All this has come upon us, yet we have not forgotten You, and we have not been false to Your covenant.
17.amp: All this is come [bo] upon us; yet have we not forgotten [shakach] You, neither have we dealt falsely in Your covenant [berith].
17.notes: kol-zot baatnu ve-lo shekhachanukha (H935, H7911): all this has come on us — and we have not FORGOTTEN You; ve-lo-shiqqarnu bi-beritekha (H1285): nor have we lied in Your covenant. The psalm's scandal: Deuteronomy 28 said defeat follows apostasy, and this generation, by its own audit (vv. 17-21), has not apostatized. Innocent suffering at national scale — Job with a flag.

18.text: Our heart has not turned back, and our steps have not strayed from Your path,
18.amp: Our heart [leb] is not turned back [achor], neither have our steps ['goings', ashur, the KJV margin] declined [natah] from Your way [orach].
18.notes: lo-nasog achor libbenu (H268, H3820): our heart has not slid back — va-tet ashurenu minni orchekha (H5186, H838, H734): nor our step — the margin's 'goings' — bent from Your path. Heart and feet, the inner and the outer test, both passed (cf. Psalm 17:5).

19.text: though You have crushed us in the place of jackals and covered us over with deep darkness.
19.amp: Though You have sore broken [dakah — crushed] us in the place [maqom] of dragons [tannin — jackals, sea-monsters], and covered [kasah] us with the shadow of death [tsalmaveth — deep darkness].
19.notes: ki dikkitanu bi-meqom tannim (H1794, H4725, H8577): though You have CRUSHED us in the place of tannim — the KJV's dragons, the WEB's jackals: the haunt of scavengers, a ruined field after battle (Isaiah 34:13). va-tekhas alenu be-tsalmavet (H3680, H6757): and covered us with tsalmavet, the death-shadow of Psalm 23:4 — here with no rod and staff in sight.

20.text: Had we forgotten our God's name, or stretched out our palms toward some foreign god,
20.amp: If we have forgotten [shakach] the name [shem] of our God [Elohim], or stretched out [paras — spread] our hands [kaph — palms] to a strange [zur — foreign] god [El];
20.notes: im-shakhachnu shem Elohenu (H7911, H8034, H430): IF we had forgotten the name of our God — va-niphros kappenu le-el zar (H6566, H3709, H410, H2114): or spread our palms to a foreign god — the prayer-posture of Psalm 143:6 aimed at the wrong altar. The oath-form: 'if we have ... then let God' — and verse 21 supplies the 'then'.

21.text: would God not search this out? For He knows the secrets of the heart.
21.amp: Shall not God [Elohim] search this out [chaqar]? for He knows [yada] the secrets of the heart [leb].
21.notes: ha-lo Elohim yachaqor-zot (H430, H2713): would God not SEARCH this out — chaqar, Psalm 139:1's searching; ki-hu yodea taalumot leb (H3045, H3820): for He knows the hidden things of the heart. The people submit their innocence to the one Auditor who cannot be fooled: a bold move, and the psalm makes it without flinching.

22.text: No — for Your sake we are being killed all day long; we are reckoned as sheep for slaughter.
22.amp: Yea, for Your sake are we killed [harag] all the day [yom] long; we are counted [chashab — reckoned] as sheep [tson] for the slaughter.
22.notes: ki-alekha horagnu khol-ha-yom (H2026, H3117): for YOUR sake we are killed all the day — not despite faithfulness but because of it — nechshabnu ke-tson tibchah (H2803, H6629): reckoned as sheep of slaughter. Paul quotes the verse whole in Romans 8:36, between 'who shall separate us' and 'more than conquerors': the church's suffering is this psalm's, and the answer Paul gives is the one the psalm was waiting for.

23.text: Wake up! Why do You sleep, O Lord? Rouse Yourself; do not cast us off forever!
23.amp: Awake [ur], why sleep [yashen] You, O Lord [Adonai]? arise [quts — rouse Yourself], cast us not off [zanach] for ever [netsach].
23.notes: urah lamah tishan Adonai (H5782, H3462, H136): WAKE UP — why do You sleep, Lord? — the boldest line in the psalm, and Psalm 121:4 has already said He does not slumber; the psalmist knows that and says it anyway, because it feels like sleep; haqitsah al-tiznach la-netsach (H6974, H2186, H5331): rouse Yourself, do not reject forever. Jesus asleep in the boat (Mark 4:38) is this verse acted out, and the disciples' 'carest thou not?' is its tone.

24.text: Why do You keep Your face hidden, forgetting our affliction and the pressure we are under?
24.amp: Wherefore hide [satar] You Your face [panim], and forget [shakach] our affliction [oni] and our oppression?
24.notes: lamah-phanekha tastir (H6440, H5641): why hide Your face — tishkach onyenu ve-lachatsenu (H7911, H6040): and FORGET our affliction and our squeeze — shakach, the verb the people denied of themselves in verses 17 and 20, now turned as a question on God. The two forgettings face each other across the psalm.

25.text: For our soul has sunk to the dust; our belly is pressed flat against the ground.
25.amp: For our soul [nephesh] is bowed down [shuach] to the dust [afar]: our belly [beten] cleaves [dabaq — clings] unto the earth [eretz].
25.notes: ki shachah le-aphar naphshenu (H7743, H6083, H5315): our soul has SUNK to the dust — dabeqah la-arets bitnenu (H1692, H776, H990): our belly clings to the ground — the posture of the serpent's curse (Genesis 3:14) and of a man face-down before an executioner. Psalm 119:25's line, in the plural.

26.text: Rise up as our help, and ransom us for the sake of Your covenant love.
26.amp: Arise [qum] for our help, and redeem [padah — ransom] us for Your mercies' [chesed — covenant love] sake.
26.notes: qumah ezratah lanu (H6965): RISE UP — 'a help for us', the margin's literal; u-phedenu le-maan chasdekha (H6299, H2617): and RANSOM us for the sake of Your chesed. The last word of the psalm is covenant love — the only ground left when innocence has been pleaded and the face is still hidden. No answer comes inside the psalm; Romans 8 is where the church reads the answer.
